art.title: The Threatened Swan
art.credit: Public domain · image via Wikimedia Commons (Rijksmuseum)
art.story: A swan rears up with its wings spread wide and its beak open, hissing at a dog that swims across the pond towards its nest in the reeds. Beside its feet lies an egg. Jan Asselijn painted it as a scene from nature, life-size. After his death someone wrote words on it: on the egg, "Holland", and by the dog, "the enemy of the state". The swan became a fierce statesman defending his country. In 1800 it was the very first painting bought for the national museum that became the Rijksmuseum.
